meta.title: Who really said "Our strategy in going after this army is very simple. First we are going to cut it off, and then we are going to kill it"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Colin Powell really said it — Pentagon briefing, 23 January 1991. UPI quoted it that day; the wire and popular renderings differ. Sources and context.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Our strategy in going after this army is very simple. First we are going to cut it off, and then we are going to kill it'?
meta.ogDescription: Genuine Powell, Pentagon, 23 January 1991 — with Cheney beside him. The circulating wording differs from what the wire filed that day.

answer.label: Spoken by
answer.authorDates: 1937–2021 · U.S. Army general, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff 1989–1993
answer.sourceLine: Powell said it at a Pentagon news briefing on 23 January 1991, standing beside Defense Secretary Dick Cheney, and United Press International quoted him that same day ↗; C-SPAN still holds the tape of the briefing ↗. The attribution is solid — but the renderings of the wording differ: the reporter in the room filed it as “Our strategy to go after this army is very, very simple,” contractions and all, while the form the quote sites carry reads “in going after … very simple.” Powell’s own recollection years later lands between the two.

source.excerpt: Our strategy to go after this army is very, very simple. First, we’re going to cut it off, and then we’re going to kill it. To cut it off, that began last week when we started to go after the nerve center, the brains of the operation, the command and control of the operation, and the lines of communication that come out of Baghdad and other places in the country.
trail: UPI filed the line the same day ↗, under Eliot Brenner’s byline, quoting Powell directly and running the phrase in the headline.
C-SPAN catalogues the video ↗ as “Defense Department News Briefing,” 23 January 1991, with Cheney and Powell speaking to reporters on the progress of the operation against Iraq.
Powell confirmed it himself years later: “I used a line I had rehearsed” ↗ — and, he added, “that became the headline.”
Wikiquote records the circulating form ↗ with the same citation — a remark as Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff at a Pentagon press briefing, 23 January 1991.
source.excerptNote: This is the passage as United Press International transcribed it on the day, a week into the coalition campaign against Iraq. The famous sentence is the second one; the third is Powell explaining what “cut it off” actually meant, and it is almost never quoted.

author.name: Colin Powell
author.heading: Who was Colin Powell?
author.metaLine: 1937–2021 · Four-star general, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff & 65th U.S. Secretary of State
author.bio: Colin Luther Powell was born in Harlem on 5 April 1937 and rose through the U.S. Army to four-star rank, serving as Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff from 1 October 1989 to 30 September 1993 — the job he held when the Gulf War began. He later became the 65th Secretary of State, serving from January 2001 to January 2005, and died on 18 October 2021 in Bethesda, Maryland. He was an unusually deliberate communicator: he told an interviewer that whenever he faced the press he was speaking to five audiences at once, the reporter asking the question being the least important of them.

misattribution.heading: Right man, drifting words
misattribution.intro: Nobody else is seriously in the frame for this one — the divergence here is not in who said it but in how it gets written down. Three small things separate the renderings.

items.why: The circulating text reads “in going after … very simple” and “we are going to.” The reporter who was in the room filed it as “Our strategy to go after this army is very, very simple. First, we’re going to cut it off, and then we’re going to kill it” (UPI, 23 January 1991 ↗) — doubled “very,” contractions and all. Which came first we do not claim: the tape (C-SPAN 151355) would settle it, and we have not transcribed it.

Interviewed for the 25th anniversary of Desert Storm, Powell said: “I used a line I had rehearsed. I said our strategy in going after the Iraqi army was very, very simple. ‘First we’re going to cut it off, and then we’re going to kill it’” (MOAA ↗). His memory splits the difference: the doubled “very” and the contractions match the wire, while the opening — “in going after” — matches the form the quote sites carry.

They reproduce the smoothed sentence with no citation attached at all — the Goodreads entry ↗ carries only the standard notice that quotes are member-contributed and not verified. That is how a real quote ends up looking as flimsy as a fabricated one.

misattribution.truthLine: The attribution itself is not in doubt: Powell said it at the Pentagon on 23 January 1991 with Dick Cheney beside him, and C-SPAN still holds the video of the briefing ↗. What varies between renderings is the opening clause, a doubled “very” and two apostrophes.

context.heading: Why this line landed
lead: Days of air war in, the press had turned. Powell later said the early euphoria over cruise missiles lasted about a week before reporters were on him with “Aha, you’re not getting it done” — so he told Cheney the two of them had to go down and calm it. The sentence that did the calming was not improvised: Powell had rehearsed it, and a Duke Law tribute recounts him saying it was crafted in advance to send a clear message ↗ to Americans, allies and the Iraqi army alike.

It worked exactly as designed. “That became the headline,” Powell recalled — and it did, almost literally: UPI ran the phrase in its headline that day ↗. It is a rare case of a soundbite whose author will tell you plainly that he built it to be one.
detailsBody: Asked about handling the press during Desert Storm, Powell explained his standing method: “When I was talking to the press, I always knew I had five audiences. The least important was the reporter asking the question.” The other four were the American people, the enemy, coalition partners with sons and daughters under U.S. command, and the troops themselves watching on the Armed Forces Network. That framing explains the shape of the line — short, concrete, and impossible to soften in translation.
Powell told the same interviewer that he knew the troops “listened just as hard as Saddam Hussein might listen.”
context.pull: That became the headline. That became the dominating theme for the next several weeks.

schema.verdictNote: Attribution traced to a primary source. The wording varies between renderings: the same-day wire transcription (see alternateName) reads "Our strategy to go after this army is very, very simple," with contractions, where the popular form reads "in going after ... very simple."

sourcesVerified.claim: UPI's same-day dispatch (by Eliot Brenner, 23 January 1991) quotes Powell: "Our strategy to go after this army is very, very simple. First, we're going to cut it off, and then we're going to kill it. To cut it off, that began last week when we started to go after the nerve center, the brains of the operation, the command and control of the operation, and the lines of communication that come out of Baghdad and other places in the country." It also describes the hour-long Cheney/Powell briefing a week into the coalition war against Iraq.

C-SPAN's program page (ID 151355) records a "Defense Department News Briefing" with event date 23 January 1991, at which Defense Secretary Cheney and General Powell, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, spoke to reporters on the progress of the military operation against Iraq.

Powell, interviewed for the 25th anniversary of Desert Storm, says of the [Jan. 23, 1991] press conference: "And I used a line I had rehearsed. I said our strategy in going after the Iraqi army was very, very simple. 'First we're going to cut it off, and then we're going to kill it.' That became the headline. That became the dominating theme for the next several weeks." The same interview contains his "five audiences" remark about talking to the press and the line that troops "listened just as hard as Saddam Hussein might listen."

Wikiquote's Colin Powell page carries "Our strategy in going after this army is very simple. First we are going to cut it off, and then we are going to kill it," cited to a remark as Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff at a Pentagon press briefing (23 January 1991).

Wikiquote's Gulf War page carries the full two-sentence quote — "Our strategy in going after this army is very simple. First we are going to cut it off, and then we are going to kill it." — attributed to Colin Powell, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Pentagon press briefing (23 January 1991); the same citation line its Colin Powell page uses.

Goodreads reproduces "Our strategy in going after this army is very simple. First we are going to cut it off, and then we are going to kill it" credited to Colin Powell with no book or publication cited, under the standard notice that quotes are member-contributed and not verified by Goodreads.

Charlie Dunlap's Duke Law "Lawfire" tribute (18 October 2021) quotes the New York Times rendering — "Our strategy in going after this army is very simple," he said. "First, we're going to cut it off, and then we're going to kill it." — and recounts Powell telling him the comment was not made off-the-cuff but carefully crafted in advance to send a clear message to America, its allies and the Iraqis.

Wikipedia gives Colin Luther Powell's birth as 5 April 1937 in Harlem, New York City; death 18 October 2021 in Bethesda, Maryland; service as Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff from 1 October 1989 to 30 September 1993; rank of four-star general; and service as Secretary of State from 20 January 2001 to 26 January 2005.
